Dhamani, ‘reed,’ appears to denote ‘pipe’ in a passage of the Rigveda and in a citation appearing in the nirukta. In the Atharvaveda it denotes, perhaps, ‘artery’ or ‘vein,’ or more generally ‘intestinal channel,’ being coupled in some passages with hirā.
Foot notes ii. 11, 8.

Dhāman denotes in the Rigveda and later ‘dwelling’ and ‘house,’ or sometimes its inmates. The word is also found in the sense of ‘ordinance,’ ‘law,’ expressing much the same as Dharman, especially in conjunction with Rta, ‘eternal order.’ Hillebrandt sees in one passage the sense of nakṣatra.
